plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded three-dimensional cutaway drawing of a domed room built as a half-ellipsoid on a circular base. The outer shell carries a blue-to-white gradient and is cut away at the front so the viewer looks into the interior, where the inner surface and the floor are shaded warm tan; a thick gray band forms the base slab beneath the floor. Two small dark points on the floor mark the foci, labeled F' on the left and F on the right. A fan of dark blue segments with arrowheads leaves F', rises at a range of angles to strike the inside of the curved dome at several separated points, and reflects back down, every one arriving at F. The paths cross one another mid-room, and no two share a bounce point. Drawing many distinct routes between the same pair of labeled points emphasizes that the convergence holds no matter which direction a ray sets out in. The illustration accounts for the acoustics of a whispering chamber, where a person speaking softly at one focus of an elliptical dome is heard clearly by a listener at the other.

elements: transparent half-ellipsoid dome shell with blue top shading fading to pale blue-white near the lower sides
front cutaway opening in the dome so the interior floor and ray paths are visible
dark blue outer rim arc following the top silhouette of the dome
thin white highlight band just inside the top rim
pale interior curved dome surface visible behind the ray paths
warm tan elliptical floor disk at the base of the dome
thick dark gray circular base slab beneath the tan floor
black front lip of the base slab with lighter gray top edge
subtle gray horizontal interior guide arcs across the back half of the dome and floor
left focus point on the floor labeled F'
right focus point on the floor labeled F
fan of dark blue outgoing sound ray segments starting at F'
distinct reflection points on the inside of the dome, one for each ray path
fan of dark blue reflected sound ray segments ending at F
dark blue arrowheads on each outgoing segment showing travel away from F'
dark blue arrowheads on each reflected segment showing travel toward F
highlight styling for the currently selected single ray path, including brighter stroke, enlarged reflection marker, and dimmed unselected paths
animated pulse markers traveling from F' to the dome reflection point and then to F

interactions.teaches: Selecting any one launch direction shows that its reflected path still reaches the other focus, so the result is not tied to a special central ray

interactions.label: Play sound pulses
interactions.teaches: Sound leaves one focus, reflects once from the ellipsoidal ceiling, and converges at the other focus as a moving wave path rather than as a static line drawing

interactions.label: Ray view
interactions.teaches: Comparing one route with the full fan reveals that the focus-to-focus reflection property is systematic across many launch angles

demo_steps.title: Full fan of reflected paths
demo_steps.narration: The initial view matches the textbook figure: several rays leave F', strike different parts of the dome, and all return to F. The crossing lines emphasize that the same endpoint is reached from many different launch angles.

demo_steps.title: Inspect one chosen route
demo_steps.narration: Switch to a single ray and click a path. Its launch segment, reflection point, and return segment are isolated so the reflection from the dome to the second focus is easy to follow.

demo_steps.title: Return to the whole chamber effect
demo_steps.narration: Switch back to all rays and play the pulse animation. The moving pulses bounce once and arrive together near F, illustrating the whispering-chamber convergence.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use world coordinates with +X screen-right, +Y vertical up, and +Z depth away from the viewer. Dome/floor footprint spans about X = -3.4 to +3.4 and Z = -1.9 to +1.9; dome height Y = 0 to 2.15. Model the visible reflection cross-section in the central vertical plane Z=0 as the upper half of an ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 with a = 3.2 and b = 2.1, y >= 0. The foci lie on the floor at F' = (-c, 0.08, 0) and F = (+c, 0.08, 0), where c = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) ≈ 2.41. Use 7 reflection points on the dome cross-section at ellipse parameters theta ≈ 28°, 45°, 62°, 82°, 104°, 128°, and 150°, with point P(theta) = (a cos theta, b sin theta, 0). Each ray path is the polyline F' -> P(theta) -> F; for all such points, |F'P| + |PF| ≈ 2a, giving the equal-distance ellipse property. The left and right focus points are small dark navy spheres or disks, radius about 0.07 world units, located on the tan floor near the front-facing central plane; labels F' and F sit just below and slightly outward from their points in dark text. Ray strokes are dark blue #003f73 or #004b80, thickness about 0.035 world units, with small triangular/cone arrowheads midway along both outgoing and reflected segments. Selected ray color should brighten to #006bb6 or #00a3ff and thicken about 1.6x; unselected rays in single-ray mode should be hidden or faded to 15% opacity. Dome shell colors: upper rim/deep edge #006c9f, main transparent blue #1aa7d9, pale highlight #dce8e8, opacity roughly 0.35-0.55. Interior/floor colors: tan floor #f1d39a with cream center #ffe1ad; interior gray-tan arcs #7f7f70 at low opacity. Base slab is a short cylinder or flattened disk, height about 0.35, with front face dark gray #4f4f4f, black outline #202020, and light gray top lip #cfcfcf. Orient the base as a horizontal disk in the XZ plane; because of the camera it should appear as a wide ellipse, with the front slab lip visible below the tan floor. The dome should read as a half-bowl cutaway: keep the rear and side surface visible, leave enough front opening/opacity for the rays and foci to be unobstructed.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the dome as a clipped upper ellipsoid mesh with transparent material and a custom vertical color gradient, plus separate curve strokes for silhouette rims and highlight bands so the outline remains crisp. Draw rays as TubeGeometry or thick screen-space lines; attach cone arrowheads aligned to segment tangents. Implement click picking per complete two-segment ray path, not per individual segment, so selecting either segment highlights the full F' -> reflection point -> F route. For the sound animation, move small glowing spheres or expanding ring pulses along each polyline with constant total normalized progress; in all-rays mode launch one pulse on each path so they converge near F together. Keep labels as billboarding text sprites anchored near the floor and always facing the camera.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click for an outgoing sound ray from F': the learner selects one path and its reflection point and return segment to F are highlighted, making clear that different launch angles still arrive at the other focus.
- Animation for sound propagation: the learner plays pulses leaving F', bouncing once off the ellipsoidal dome, and converging at F, making clear the dynamic reflection path behind the whispering-chamber effect.
- Toggle between single-ray and all-rays views: the learner switches from one highlighted route to the full fan of reflected paths, making clear that the focus-to-focus property is systematic rather than a coincidence of one ray.

authoredContext:
Many real-world situations can be represented by ellipses, including orbits of planets, satellites, moons and comets, and shapes of boat keels, rudders, and some airplane wings. A medical device called a lithotripter uses elliptical reflectors to break up kidney stones by generating sound waves. Some buildings, called whispering chambers, are designed with elliptical domes so that a person whispering at one focus can easily be heard by someone standing at the other focus. This occurs because of the acoustic properties of an ellipse. When a sound wave originates at one focus of a whispering chamber, the sound wave will be reflected off the elliptical dome and back to the other focus. See the figure. In the whisper chamber at the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago, two people standing at the foci—about 43 feet apart—can hear each other whisper. When these chambers are placed in unexpected places, such as the ones inside Bush International Airport in Houston and Grand Central Terminal in New York City, they can induce surprised reactions among travelers.

Sound waves are reflected between foci in an elliptical room, called a whispering chamber.

An illustration of a semi-ellipsoidal dome with two focal points, F and F'. Blue lines with arrows represent rays originating from focal point F'. These rays reflect off the inner curved surface of the dome and converge at the second focal point F, demonstrating the reflective property of an ellipse.

discrepancies: The dome is noticeably flatter and wider than the taller, more hemispherical cap in the source figure.
The generated ray fan has more paths and more crisscrossing lines than the source, making the interior busier and less faithful to the original composition.
The source has a stronger layered/double blue-purple outer dome outline, while the generated dome rim is simplified mostly to blue and white arcs.
The base ring is thicker and darker in the generated figure, with a more pronounced black front lip than in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable as the whispering chamber diagram with correct foci, dome, base, and reflected rays, but the dome proportions and ray density differ from the source.
action_items: Make the dome taller and less flattened to better match the source silhouette.
Reduce the number of ray paths or choose reflection points closer to the source arrangement to reduce visual clutter.
Add a more faithful double outer rim with the darker blue/purple layered outline visible in the reference.
Lighten and slightly reduce the base lip thickness to better match the original base ring.

feedback.rationale: The figure is conceptually correct with very high scores and only minor scale/styling discrepancies, so further iteration is unlikely to provide meaningful improvement.
